talk: A SAFE (simple agreement for future equity) lets an investor give you money now and get shares later, at your next priced round. A valuation cap sets the most they'll pay, and a discount gives them a cheaper price than new investors. They get whichever deal is better for them.

terms.meaning: Money now, shares later, at the next priced round.
The highest valuation the SAFE turns into shares at.
A percentage off the price new investors pay.

questions.prompt: An investor gives you $500,000 on a SAFE with a $5M post-money cap. If the next round values the club above $5M, what share does the SAFE turn into?
questions.hint: With a post-money cap, divide the money by the cap.
whyNot: 50% would mean the investor paid half the cap. They paid $500,000 / $5M = 10% of it.

questions.prompt: At the next round, new investors pay $2 a share. The SAFE has a 20% discount. What price does the SAFE investor pay with the discount?
whyNot: $0.40 is the discount, not the price.
$2 is what new investors pay. The SAFE gets 20% off.
$2 + $0.40 = $2.40 adds the discount. It comes off.

questions.prompt: The cap works out at $1.25 a share and the discount at $1.60. What price does the SAFE investor get?
questions.hint: They get whichever is better for them.
working: They get the lower of the two prices: $1.25.
For the same money they get $2 / $1.25 = 1.6 times as many shares as a new investor. That's their reward for backing you early.
whyNot: $1.25 + $1.60 = $2.85 adds them. The investor gets the lower of the two, not the sum.
$2 is what new investors pay. SAFE investors are rewarded for coming in early.
$1.60 is higher than the cap price, so the investor takes the cap.

penalty.prompt: An investor puts {inv} into a SAFE with a {cap} post-money cap. What share of the club does it turn into? (As a percentage.)
penalty.hint: With a post-money cap, divide the money by the cap.

traps.why: That treats the cap as a pre-money. With a post-money cap, divide by the cap itself.

call.title: Money for the pitch
call.prompt: The pitch must be repaired in the next month or matches get cancelled. It costs $1M. Option one: a SAFE with a $10M cap. Option two: a SAFE with a $4M cap from an investor who can wire money today. Option three: a priced round at a $6M pre-money, which takes six weeks and $50,000 of legal fees, closing a stand while you wait.

options.label: SAFE with a $10M cap
options.result: Good call. At most $1M / $10M = 10% of the club, and the money arrives this week.

options.label: SAFE with a $4M cap
options.result: $1M / $4M = 25% for the same money. A low cap is an expensive way to raise fast.

options.label: Priced round at $6M pre-money
options.result: $6M + $1M = $7M post-money, so $1M / $7M = about 14%, plus $50,000 of legal fees and a closed stand while you wait.

takeaway: A SAFE turns into shares later. A high cap is good for you, a low cap is good for the investor.
